Temporal.DateTime.name: Temporal.DateTime
Temporal.DateTime.description: ISO8601 datetime string. Epoch wire values keep this scalar and declare x-temporal-format (unix, unix_millis, unix_micros, unix_nanos) on the property; the unit is never guessed from digit count.

Customer.name: Customer
Customer.comment: A customer an invoice is billed to.

Invoice.name: Invoice
Invoice.comment:
An invoice a person reads out by its number (D56, D103's step 4): each
customer's invoices are numbered from 1 each UTC year, INV-2026-0042,
so a label is unique within its customer, which the index holds. A
refused create takes no number, and a delete leaves a gap. An invoice
made before the table numbered has none until assignNumber gives it the
next number of the year it was made in, read from its createdAt.

fields.name: numberSeq
fields.description: The instance's number in its count, from 1; absent until it is numbered.

fields.name: number
fields.description: The number as the format prints it, unique within its scope; absent until it is numbered.

InvoiceNumberCounts.name: InvoiceNumberCounts
InvoiceNumberCounts.comment: On a table, one row per count, kept for the table as a whole: the last number it gave and the config it counted under. A delete of a row leaves it where it was, so a delete leaves a gap; a row whose config is not the use's counts from 1 again.

fields.name: scope
fields.description: What the count runs per: the key of the scope relation's target and the UTC year, each the config counts by, joined with a slash, or * for a count of the whole table.

fields.name: last
fields.description: The last number the count gave.

fields.name: counting
fields.description: The format, the scope and the reset the count was made under, as JSON.

Ticket.name: Ticket
